input.question: How can I go to sleep extremely hungry/thirsty yet wake up and not feel the hunger/thirst at all?
input.ground_truth: After the energy of the food you consumed is used up, your blood sugar drops and the body enters a fasting state. The liver releases small doses of glucose by breaking down glycogen to maintain your blood sugar (in your case while sleeping). So when you wake up your blood sugar is at the right level and you don't feel hungry.

Question: How can I go to sleep extremely hungry/thirsty yet wake up and not feel the hunger/thirst at all?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you’re a teddy bear at night. If you go to bed feeling super hungry or super thirsty, your body knows you need food or water. But when you’re sleeping, you don’t really notice those feelings as much because your brain is resting and dreaming.

It’s like when you’re playing and then you get tired and close your eyes. While you’re sleeping, you don’t think about being thirsty or hungry until you wake up. When you wake up, your body might remember it was hungry or thirsty, but sometimes you don’t feel it right away because your body was busy resting and fixing itself while you were asleep.

So, it’s like your body puts the “hungry” or “thirsty” feeling on pause while you sleep, but it comes back when you open your eyes!
